subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A symmetric matrix is positive definite exactly when
solution_latex: For symmetric A, xᵀAx>0 for all nonzero x iff every eigenvalue is positive.
common_mistake: Positive trace or determinant alone is insufficient.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A positive semidefinite matrix may have eigenvalues
solution_latex: Semidefinite permits zero curvature directions.
common_mistake: Strict positivity characterizes positive definite.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: For skew-symmetric K, xᵀKx equals
solution_latex: The scalar equals its transpose, which is its negative, so it must be zero.
common_mistake: This holds for every real x.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: The matrix representing 2x²+6xy+5y² is
solution_latex: The cross term is 2a12xy, so a12=3.
common_mistake: Split the cross coefficient equally across symmetric off-diagonals.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: An indefinite quadratic form takes
solution_latex: Indefinite means there are directions with opposite signs.
common_mistake: A zero direction alone indicates semidefiniteness, not indefiniteness.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Sylvester’s criterion for symmetric positive definiteness requires
solution_latex: Every leading principal minor must be strictly positive.
common_mistake: The full determinant is only the last condition.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Which symmetric diagonal matrices are positive semidefinite?
solution_latex: Diagonal eigenvalues are the diagonal entries; PSD means each is nonnegative.
common_mistake: One negative entry makes the form negative along that axis.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: At a stationary point, a positive-definite Hessian implies
solution_latex: Positive curvature in every direction gives a strict local minimum.
common_mistake: The stationary-point condition is also needed.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Only which part of A affects xᵀAx?
solution_latex: xᵀAx equals xᵀ((A+Aᵀ)/2)x because the skew part vanishes.
common_mistake: A nonsymmetric representation can be symmetrized.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: If A is positive definite, then A is
solution_latex: All eigenvalues are positive and hence nonzero.
common_mistake: Positive definite is stronger than invertible.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: For q=3x²+4xy+2y², enter the off-diagonal entry in its symmetric matrix.
solution_latex: The cross coefficient is 2a12=4, so a12=2.
common_mistake: Halve the xy coefficient.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter xᵀAx for A=diag(2,3) and x=(1,2).
solution_latex: The form is 2·1²+3·2²=2+12=14.
common_mistake: Square vector components.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A symmetric 2×2 matrix has eigenvalues 4 and −1. Enter the number of positive eigenvalues.
solution_latex: Exactly one eigenvalue is positive; the form is indefinite.
common_mistake: Count signs with multiplicity.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter the smallest eigenvalue of diag(5,0,2).
solution_latex: Diagonal entries are eigenvalues, and the smallest is zero.
common_mistake: PSD need not be strictly positive.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: For A=[[2,1],[1,2]], enter its determinant.
solution_latex: det(A)=4−1=3; together with leading minor 2>0 this confirms positive definiteness.
common_mistake: A positive determinant alone would not suffice in higher dimensions.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter q(1,−1) for q(x,y)=x²+2xy+y².
solution_latex: q=(x+y)², so at (1,−1) it is zero.
common_mistake: This form is semidefinite, not definite.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A positive-definite 3×3 matrix has eigenvalues 1,2,a. Enter the smallest integer a allowed.
solution_latex: Positive definiteness requires a>0; the smallest positive integer is 1.
common_mistake: Zero would make it only semidefinite.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: If A has eigenvalues −2,−3, enter the number of negative eigenvalues of −A.
solution_latex: Negation changes them to 2 and 3, both positive.
common_mistake: Every eigenvalue changes sign.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter xᵀKx for any real skew-symmetric K and x.
solution_latex: The quadratic form of a real skew-symmetric matrix always vanishes.
common_mistake: Do not infer K itself is zero.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A symmetric matrix has inertia (2 positive,1 zero,3 negative). Enter its dimension.
solution_latex: Inertia counts all eigenvalue signs: 2+1+3=6.
common_mistake: Include the zero eigenvalues.
